quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never touch the operator.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when turning. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When turning, it is important to:

options.text: Look straight ahead.
Slow down after you start turning.
Reduce speed as you exit the turn.
Look through the turn toward where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Always slow down before entering the turn.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: A hard outer shell that resists impact.
A soft inner liner that absorbs impact.
A chinstrap system to keep it secure.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have a hard outer shell, a soft inner liner, a comfort liner, and a secure chinstrap. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves their arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that do not cover the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Shoes should have low heels so they do not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Only use mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Check your mirrors especially:

options.text: On long trips.
When riding through an intersection.
When following another vehicle.
Before you slow down or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you slow down or stop.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before stopping at an intersection, before changing lanes, and before slowing down.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
In any part of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and stay straight. Brake gently on the good tire. As you slow, move to the road edge, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Ride faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about your lane position at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Apply brakes automatically.
Alert you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. When you apply maximum pressure to both brakes, sensors detect wheel lock and release then re-apply pressure to maintain the best braking power.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting into a lower gear.
Speed up before shifting into a lower gear.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you that you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: You must slow down enough before shifting into a lower gear. Shifting too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: You should check traffic behind your motorcycle:

options.text: Before starting into a curve.
When approaching an intersection.
When carrying a passenger.
Before slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you slow down. Drivers behind you may not expect you to slow down or notice that you are slowing down.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Shift gears while turning.
Shift gears before turning.
Change power suddenly while turning.
Brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on slippery surfaces. You can use the front brake safely on wet pavement if you apply it gradually to prevent the wheel from locking.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.
Ride faster than usual.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Slow down and increase your following distance when riding at night. Use your high beam whenever you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious.
Takes away your ability to change direction.
Will fix itself automatically.
Is only dangerous if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes away your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a crash or serious injury. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down and lean your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Get a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Lose power to the rear wheel suddenly.
Lose power to the front wheel suddenly.
Get a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose power to the rear wheel suddenly.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt fails, the rear wheel will lose power immediately.

questions.question: What should you do to stay in control while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before you turn and lean the motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: During acceleration, a sidecar attached to a motorcycle will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
Shake uncontrollably.
Make acceleration feel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to the side of your motorcycle. When you accelerate, the sidecar will feel like it is falling behind because of its weight.
